summary.headline: Fujiyama Q2 FY27 revenue rose 130% to ₹1,307 crore, but EBITDA margin slipped to 17.1% from 18.9% in Q1 on overheads and inventory build.
summary.overview: H1 FY27 revenue reached ₹2,652 crore, roughly equal to full-year FY26 revenue of ₹2,655 crore, with H1 profit after tax of ₹98 crore (up 128%, per the transcript's stated figures). Q2 revenue grew 130% to ₹1,307 crore and PAT grew 116% to ₹223 crore. Management attributed the sequential margin dip to seasonal softness, under-absorbed fixed costs at the new Ratlam facility, higher selling and distribution spend in tier 2/3 markets, and buying tubular batteries externally after the Babal fire. Inventory rose to ₹1,230 crore from ₹910 crore in March, but inventory days fell to 99 from 123 and net working capital days to 59 from 83. Management declined to revise or restate full-year revenue guidance until Q3 results.

segments.name: Residential / retail rooftop solar (B2C, dealer-led)
segments.commentary: Management says over 85% of revenue comes from retail, household and small business customers. Around 50% of revenue is said to come from on-grid and DCR-linked subsidy customers, per the Q&A.

segments.name: Solar cells and panels
segments.commentary: Capacity is 1 GW cells and 3.5 GW panels. Management says roughly 70-80% of DCR panels sold in H1 used in-house cells, with 20-30% bought externally.

segments.name: Inverters / power electronics
segments.commentary: Capacity is 4 GW, with a 2 GW Ratlam facility commissioned in August. Covers on-grid, off-grid and hybrid types, and the company claims it has sold over 1.4 million inverters since 1996.

segments.name: Lithium-ion and tubular batteries
segments.commentary: Lithium-ion capacity is 545 MW, planned to rise to 3.5 GWh. A 1 GW tubular plant at Hardoi, UP replaces Babal capacity lost in a May fire and is due next quarter.

guidance_outlook: No revision of full-year revenue guidance this quarter; management will review guidance with Q3 results.
Management said the EBITDA margin of 17-19% would be sustainable, though it avoided aggressive guidance.
Ratlam lithium-ion battery expansion to 3.5 GWh expected next quarter; Hardoi tubular plant expected next quarter.
Ratlam 1.2 GW TOPCon cell line on track for Q1 FY28, taking cell capacity to 2.2 GW; management is pushing for an earlier launch.
Management expects a QIP resolution, subject to board approval, which could fund debt repayment.
capex_capacity: Ratlam: 2 GW power electronics commissioned in August; 2 GW solar panel line started in May.
Ratlam lithium-ion battery upsized from 2 GWh to 3 GWh, due online next quarter, taking total to 3.5 GWh.
Hardoi, UP: 1 GW tubular battery plant replacing Babal capacity, due next quarter.
Ratlam 1.2 GW TOPCon cell line on track for Q1 FY28, taking cell capacity to 2.2 GW.
Gyro Energy and Gyro Cable raised to 50% stake; these entities plan frames, ribbons, junction boxes, cables and EVA sheets in FY28. Pilot projects: 5 MW BESS at Dadri and 10 MW at Ratlam.
demand_pricing: Management says the rooftop market is about 26 GW (March 2026), against an estimated 67 GW potential, with PM Surya Ghar at over 60 lakh households and 19 GW installed.
Around 5 lakh households remain in the PM Surya Ghar phase running to March 2027; PM Surya Ghar 2.0 is under government consideration, with battery storage support reportedly proposed.
Management says the DCR cell run-rate is about 2 GW against higher demand, and that ALMM List-II from 1 January 2027 could lift DCR cell prices.
Management described the non-DCR segment as weak with no sign of improvement.
Q2 margin fell on higher overheads, but gross margin was stable across Q1 and Q2 (per management).

qa_highlights.question: How should H2 revenue growth be viewed, given that H1 growth was about 100%+ and the guidance has been stated?
qa_highlights.answer: Management declined to give H2 guidance and will revise it with Q3 results, citing market variables, DCR shortage and PM Surya Ghar 2.0 timing.

qa_highlights.question: Will EBITDA margins hold at 18-20% given backward integration?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said margins would be sustainable at roughly 18-19%, citing the consumer product mix and DCR shortage.

qa_highlights.question: Why are margins lower than solar-cell peers (around 30%)?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the peer margin spikes are temporary, and that the B2C model with a mix of panels, batteries and inverters gives steadier margins. It declined to commit to aggressive margin expansion from cell integration.

qa_highlights.question: What share of H1 DCR panels used in-house cells?
qa_highlights.answer: Management estimated 70-80% in-house and 20-30% externally sourced.

qa_highlights.question: What share of H1 revenue came from subsidy customers?
qa_highlights.answer: Management estimated about 50% of revenue from the on-grid and DCR-linked subsidy market.

qa_highlights.question: Why did other expenses rise to ₹112 crore in Q2?
qa_highlights.answer: Management cited Ratlam fixed overheads capitalised from August, higher selling and distribution spend for tier 2/3 brand visibility, and higher fuel costs.

qa_highlights.question: How much revenue came from the South, and what is the status of the expansion there?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said it would share the South revenue figure offline. It said Andhra Pradesh and Telangana are being expanded, and Maharashtra and Gujarat are served from MP.

qa_highlights.question: What is driving the debt increase and negative cash flow?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said debt rose by about ₹100 crore for the Ratlam expansion and about ₹300 crore overall, with inventory linked to doubled revenue. It also cited about ₹80 crore of damaged inventory (per the transcript) and an expected insurance claim of about ₹140 crore.

risks_watch: Inventory of ₹1,230 crore and debt of ₹851 crore, with negative free cash flow in H1 as working capital absorbed about ₹651 crore.
Policy uncertainty: ALMM List-II for DCR cells from 1 January 2027 and PM Surya Ghar 2.0 timing.
Q2 margin dip to 17.1% from 18.9% in Q1, with rising overheads from the Ratlam start-up and tier 2/3 marketing spend.
Raw material and fuel price volatility, linked to geopolitical conditions.
Commissioning timelines: Hardoi tubular, Ratlam lithium-ion and the TOPCon cell line (Q1 FY28).
Potential Chinese restrictions on solar technology transfer; management said machinery is already received.
Outcome of the QIP resolution and debt repayment plan.
Transcript quality: several figures (PAT, EBITDA, Q2 revenue split, debt amounts) are garbled or inconsistent and should be verified against the presentation.
summary.management_tone: Confident on long-term demand, brand, and integration, but cautious and evasive on forward numbers: it declined to revise FY27 revenue guidance and gave no aggressive margin or cell-capacity targets. Management attributed the margin dip to specific temporary causes such as the Babal fire, Ratlam overheads and marketing investment.

growth.why: Full-year FY27 revenue guidance was withdrawn and will be revised only after Q3 results, while EBITDA margin of 17-19% is said to be sustainable; growth is backed by commissioned Ratlam inverter capacity and several capacity additions due next quarter, but no numeric FY27 revenue guide is given.

rows.label: Margin expansion
rows.why: Management says the 17-19% EBITDA margin is sustainable and gross margin was stable Q1 to Q2, but Q2 EBITDA margin slipped to 17.1% from 18.9% on Ratlam overheads and tier 2/3 marketing, and it declined to commit to expansion from cell integration.

rows.label: Capacity expansion / commissioning
rows.why: Ratlam 2 GW inverter plant was commissioned in August, the Hardoi 1 GW tubular plant and Ratlam lithium-ion upsizing to 3.5 GWh are due next quarter, and the 1.2 GW TOPCon cell line is on track for Q1 FY28 (cell capacity to 2.2 GW from 1 GW).

rows.label: Volume growth
rows.why: H1 revenue of ₹2,652 crore is about equal to FY26 full-year revenue, and new capacity comes live next quarter, though management gave no numeric H2 guide and the non-DCR segment is weak.

rows.label: New capex announcement
rows.why: Gyro Energy and Gyro Cable raised to 50% with FY28 plans for frames, ribbons, junction boxes and cables, 5 MW and 10 MW BESS pilots are running, and the Ratlam lithium-ion line was upsized, but no new capex figure was given and DCR cell run-rate is only about 2 GW against higher demand.

rows.label: Guidance upgrade
rows.why: Management declined to revise or restate FY27 revenue guidance until Q3 results and gave no aggressive margin or cell-capacity targets.

rows.label: Guidance downgrade
rows.why: Guidance was dropped rather than reiterated, and the revision comes with Q3 results, amid policy uncertainty (ALMM List-II from 1 Jan 2027, PM Surya Ghar 2.0 timing), with about 5 lakh households left in the PM Surya Ghar phase to March 2027.

rows.label: New product launch
rows.why: Ratlam lithium-ion expansion to 3.5 GWh and the Hardoi tubular plant are due next quarter, and the Gyro Energy/Cable product set (frames, ribbons, junction boxes, cables, EVA sheets) is planned for FY28.

rows.label: Inventory and working capital unwind
rows.why: Inventory days fell to 99 from 123 and NWC days to 59 from 83, but inventory of ₹1,230 crore and debt of ₹851 crore (up about ₹300 crore) remain high against H1 working capital absorption of about ₹651 crore.

rows.label: QIP to fund debt repayment
rows.why: Management expects a QIP resolution subject to board approval, which could fund debt repayment against total debt of ₹851 crore, but no size or date was given.

rows.label: ALMM List-II and PM Surya Ghar 2.0
rows.why: ALMM List-II from 1 January 2027 could lift DCR cell prices, and PM Surya Ghar 2.0 with battery storage support is under government consideration, but neither is confirmed.

tone.note: Management was confident on long-term demand, brand and backward integration, and attributed the margin dip to temporary causes (Babal fire, Ratlam overheads, marketing), but it was cautious and evasive on forward numbers, declining to give H2 revenue guidance or aggressive margin targets.
